CHIEF COMPLAINT
Back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports left lower back pain. He had microdiscectomy surgery in November 2020 for a herniated disk that wrapped around the spinal thecal sac. He previously experienced severe nerve pain down his leg. He was on high-dose gabapentin, which was difficult to withdraw from. Currently experiencing left-sided low back pain that sometimes radiates to the right side depending on the day, generally around the surgical site. Stretching helps with the pain. Bending over makes it worse. Pain sometimes occurs randomly. Has not tried icing. Currently taking ibuprofen 800mg daily. On physical examination: no pain with forward flexion or extension, pain with weight-bearing while standing, pain with palpation to the left side around L5, no pain with palpation to the right side, normal dorsiflexion, normal range of motion, no pain down the legs. X-ray shows no fractures and proper healing at the surgical site. Assessment is muscle pull from spinal misalignment.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No nerve pain down legs.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Microdiscectomy in November 2020 for herniated disk.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen 800mg daily. Gabapentin (previously, high doses, now discontinued).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient has a significant other who encourages stretching. Has attended physical therapy at the VA previously.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Flexion: No pain. Extension: No pain. Weight-bearing: Pain while standing. Palpation: Pain at left L5, no pain on right side. Dorsiflexion: Normal. Range of motion: Normal. Lower extremities: No pain or nerve pain.

RESULTS
X-ray: No fractures. Surgical site healed properly.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Muscle pull from spinal misalignment. Prescribe meloxicam instead of ibuprofen for better pain management. Prescribe demerol. Prescribe physical therapy at the VA. Referral to pain management for consultation regarding pain management and non-narcotic options.
